surfaces: Zed desktop editor (Windows). Agent Panel with the native "Zed Agent" plus External Agents over ACP (e.g. Claude Code, Gemini CLI) and Terminal Threads (owned by the CLI, not by Zed). Threads Sidebar groups threads by project. Note: Zed is NOT a VS Code/JetBrains extension - it is a standalone editor, so there is no IDE globalStorage/state.vscdb; its state lives in its own data dir.
binaries: zed.exe (Zed desktop app). Agent work runs in-process (native agent) or in an external ACP agent process hosted by Zed.

paths: %LOCALAPPDATA%\Zed\threads\threads.db  (Windows; agent threads - the only viable activity source)
override: Zed accepts a --user-data-dir CLI flag (crates/zed/src/main.rs:262-263) which moves the whole data dir
storage.format: Standard SQLite3 file (Zed's sqlez layer is built directly on libsqlite3-sys, busy_timeout 5000ms). Schema: CREATE TABLE threads (id TEXT PRIMARY KEY, summary TEXT NOT NULL, updated_at TEXT NOT NULL, data_type TEXT NOT NULL, data BLOB NOT NULL) plus runtime ALTER TABLE columns parent_id TEXT, folder_paths TEXT, folder_paths_order TEXT, created_at TEXT. `data` = zstd (level 3) compressed JSON of the whole thread (DbThread, version "0.3.0"); data_type is "zstd" today, "json" for legacy rows. One row per thread; no per-project subdirectories.
storage.append_semantics: NOT append-only. Every save is a whole-row upsert: INSERT INTO threads (...) VALUES (...) ON CONFLICT(id) DO UPDATE SET data = excluded.data - the zstd blob is a full snapshot of the thread, replaced in place. Saves are triggered by cx.observe(thread) -> a debounced save worker that persists the latest snapshot of a burst, plus a flush on quit; saves are skipped while a response is streaming if the streaming key is unchanged. Consequence: a LogTailer/file-watcher cannot work; the adapter must poll the DB and diff snapshots per thread.
storage.session_file_naming: No per-session files. Thread identity = the `id` column (an ACP SessionId string / UUID) and `parent_id` marks Zed subagent threads. Project grouping = the `folder_paths` column (newline-joined absolute worktree paths, order in `folder_paths_order` as comma-joined indices).

fields.project: Recoverable. The `folder_paths` column holds the absolute worktree paths of the thread (newline separated); only the final path component may be published. Upstream: crates/agent/src/db.rs (save_thread_sync/list_threads), crates/util/src/path_list.rs (serialize/deserialize).
fields.model: Recoverable. The thread blob carries `model` = SerializedLanguageModel { provider, model } (e.g. "anthropic" / "claude-sonnet-4-5"). Upstream: crates/agent/src/legacy_thread.rs:45-49, crates/agent/src/db.rs:67.
fields.file_basename: Recoverable for Zed's native agent: the tool input JSON has a `path` field (read_file/edit_file/write_file/list_directory/find_path) and `command` for the terminal tool. Upstream: crates/agent/src/tools/read_file_tool.rs:161-179, edit_file_tool.rs:37-59, write_file_tool.rs:28-50, list_directory_tool.rs:24-50, terminal_tool.rs:52-56. For External Agents over ACP the file path comes from ACP ToolCall `locations` / `raw_input` (crates/acp_thread/src/acp_thread.rs:1096-1121).
fields.tool_activity: Recoverable. ToolUse entries persist the tool name plus the raw input JSON (LanguageModelToolUse { id, name, raw_input, input, is_input_complete, thought_signature }; crates/language_model_core/src/language_model_core.rs:592-608) and the matching tool_results map holds tool_use_id/tool_name/is_error/output (crates/agent/src/db.rs:303-312). Only a fixed label + basename may leave the parser.
fields.phase: NOT stored; must be derived. Pending ToolUse without a matching tool_result => RunningTools; agent text => Thinking/TerminalCandidate. No explicit phase field, no explicit turn-end/completion marker.
fields.timestamps: Only thread-level: `updated_at` and `created_at` (RFC3339 strings) on the row. Individual messages carry NO timestamps (UserMessage/AgentMessage have none: crates/agent/src/thread.rs:202-208, 287-298, 743-759), so per-turn start times and the elapsed timer can only be approximated (row updated_at at the moment a new user message is first observed, else poll time).

parser_strategy: Not line-based. Two new pieces: (1) events.rs gains `pub fn parse_zed_thread(snapshot: &serde_json::Value) -> Vec<ParsedEvent>` which maps one thread snapshot to events: `model` -> AgentDetected{sanitize(model string, [A-Za-z0-9._:-], <=64 chars)}; row `folder_paths` -> SessionMetadata{project: last component of the first worktree path, cwd: that path (internal only, used by state.rs to detect the project stack)}; messages[] walked in order: {"User":..} -> TaskStarted{started_at_ms = row updated_at at first observation, fallback now}; {"Agent":{content:[{"ToolUse":{id,name,input}}]}} -> TrackedToolStarted{call_id:id, activity{label: classify_tool(name, input.command), file: basename(input.path), language: language_from_file(basename)}}; {"Agent":{tool_results:{id:..}}} -> TrackedToolFinished{call_id:id}; {"Agent":{content:[{"Thinking":..}]}} -> Thinking{reasoning: None} (never forward reasoning text); {"Agent":{content:[{"Text":..}]}} -> TerminalCandidate. (2) a new src/zed.rs reader owns the SQLite access + diffing: open the DB read-only, `SELECT id, parent_id, folder_paths, updated_at, created_at, data_type, data FROM threads`, zstd::bulk::decompress each `data` (cap 32 MB), parse with parse_zed_thread, and emit ONLY the delta versus the previous snapshot for that thread id (per-thread cursor = message count + set of seen tool_use ids), so a poll never republishes the same tool call. The reader is driven by a 1.5-2 s poller (not the LogTailer); a notify Modify event on threads.db may be used only as a debounced wake-up hint. Because every thread in every project lives in one file, the per-session key must become per thread: use a synthetic key `threads.db#<thread_id>` (PathBuf) so state.rs's HashMap<PathBuf, SessionState> keeps one session per thread unchanged; the path-substring subagent matching in state.rs does not apply to Zed, so subagent threads (parent_id NOT NULL) are simply reported as separate threads.
discodex_plan:
PROVIDER: reuse the existing `Provider::Zed` variant (display_name "Zed AI"); flip `has_session_tracking()` to include Zed. No new enum variant needed.

SESSION ROOT (exact): `dirs::data_local_dir().join("Zed").join("threads")` -> %LOCALAPPDATA%\Zed\threads (upstream paths::data_dir() == dirs::data_local_dir().join("Zed")). `dirs` is already a dependency. Windows-only build, so no macOS/Linux variants needed (keep them behind cfg for future use).

is_session_log: `Provider::Zed => lower_filename == "threads.db"` (single file, no per-project subdirs).

parse_line_for strategy: the contract is line-based, so parse_line_for(Zed, line) can only accept a single whole-thread snapshot; implement `parse_zed_thread(&Value) -> Vec<ParsedEvent>` in events.rs and have the new zed.rs reader call it per row, diffing per thread. Mapping: row.folder_paths -> SessionMetadata; blob.model -> AgentDetected; messages[User] -> TaskStarted; messages[Agent].ToolUse -> TrackedToolStarted; tool_results[id] -> TrackedToolFinished; content[Thinking] -> Thinking{reasoning: None}; content[Text] -> TerminalCandidate. There is no Completed marker upstream: completion is expressed via TerminalCandidate + Discodex's existing 4 s terminal debounce (or `discard_stale_active`).

WATCHER/MAIN CHANGES (the format is NOT append-only JSONL - extra machinery required): 1) New dependency `rusqlite = { version = "0.3x", features = ["bundled"] }` (Windows has no system SQLite, so `bundled` is mandatory; it compiles the SQLite C amalgamation with cc: +1-2 min cold build, ~+1.5-2 MB binary). `zstd`, `serde_json`, `dirs` are already present. 2) watcher.rs: keep LogTailer/recent_logs untouched for the 4 JSONL providers; add `zed::poll_once(&mut ZedReader) -> Vec<(SessionKey, Vec<ParsedEvent>)>` that opens the DB read-only (SQLITE_OPEN_READ_ONLY, busy_timeout ~1500 ms), reads the table, decompresses+parses rows, and diffs against per-thread cursors. On SQLITE_BUSY/locked, corrupt zstd, unknown data_type or unknown blob "version": skip the row, keep the previous cursor (never advance on failure), and continue - fail safe, never crash the tray. 3) main.rs: start a dedicated poller task (e.g. 1.5-2 s tick) that feeds the same event channel the log watcher uses; do NOT route threads.db through LogTailer. 4) state.rs: no change needed if a synthetic per-thread key (threads.db#<thread_id>) is used as the session key; note that state.rs's subagent path-substring matching does not apply to Zed UUID thread ids.

UNIT TESTS TO ADD (5): (a) zed_thread_snapshot_maps_to_safe_events - synthetic snapshot with an edit_file ToolUse {path:"C:\\work\\Discodex\\src\\tray.rs"} + tool_result + final Text -> expect TrackedToolStarted{label:"Editing files", file:"tray.rs", language:"Rust"}, TrackedToolFinished, TerminalCandidate, SessionMetadata{project:"Discodex"}, AgentDetected{"claude-sonnet-4-5"}. (b) MANDATORY PRIVACY: zed_prompts_responses_and_tool_output_are_never_forwarded - the snapshot contains "PRIVATE_PROMPT", "PRIVATE_OLD/NEW", "PRIVATE_TOOL_OUTPUT", "PRIVATE_FINAL_ANSWER"; assert the serialized ParsedEvent set contains none of those substrings, that Thinking carries reasoning: None, and that the tool label is a fixed string from classify_tool. (c) zed_model_and_project_are_derived_without_leaking_paths - model {provider,model} -> AgentDetected with only the model id; folder_paths -> project = last path component only (full path must not appear in any published field). (d) zed_snapshot_diff_never_repeats_events - polling the identical snapshot twice yields no second TrackedToolStarted; a snapshot with one extra ToolUse yields exactly one new event (guards the 1.5 s poll against spamming Discord). FORMAT-CHURN RISK / FAIL SAFE: (1) the blob's internal "version" (DbThread::VERSION = "0.3.0" today) is bumped by Zed on schema changes - parse leniently, and on an unknown version skip the row rather than guess (keep the existing focused window/exe detection for Zed as the fallback). (2) data_type may be "json" for legacy rows - support both, skip anything else. (3) threads-table columns are added at runtime via ALTER TABLE; a future rename makes the SELECT fail - catch the error, log once, and fall back to focused detection instead of crashing. (4) rows are whole-snapshot rewrites, so a read can land mid-transaction - read-only + busy_timeout, retry on the next tick, and only commit the diff cursor after a fully successful parse. (5) the DB contains the full conversation of every thread of every project - read only rows whose updated_at is recent (e.g. last 10 minutes, parsed from RFC3339), never persist any of it, and never publish `summary` (the model-written thread title).

risks: NEW DEPENDENCY + NEW INGESTION ARCHITECTURE: threads.db is a SQLite file whose payload is a zstd blob, and it is rewritten in place, so the existing LogTailer/recent_logs/parse_line_for(line) contract does not apply. Discodex needs rusqlite (bundled SQLite C, +1-2 min cold build, ~+1.5-2 MB binary) plus a poll-and-diff reader and a per-thread session key. This is a materially bigger change than the four existing JSONL adapters.

NO PER-EVENT TIMESTAMPS: messages carry no timestamp, only the row's updated_at/created_at (RFC3339). The elapsed timer can only be approximated from the updated_at of the save that first contained the user message (error = Zed save latency + poll interval, typically 1-3 s), and turn boundaries are inferred. Codex/Claude Code give exact task_started times, so the timer will be visibly less precise.

NO EXPLICIT COMPLETION MARKER: there is no task_complete event upstream; completion must ride on TerminalCandidate + Discodex's 4 s terminal debounce or the stale-session reaper, so a turn that ends with only tool calls can look 'running' until the staleness timeout.

WHOLE-ROW REWRITES: a read can land while Zed is mid-transaction -> SQLITE_BUSY / partially written blob. Mitigations: read-only open, busy_timeout, skip-and-retry, never advance the diff cursor on a failed parse.

FORMAT CHURN: the blob's internal version string (DbThread::VERSION, "0.3.0" today) and the data_type tag ("zstd"/"json") and the threads-table column set all change over time; a rename makes the SELECT fail. Fail safe: catch the error, log once, skip the provider and keep the existing focused-app detection for Zed.

PRIVACY: the blob contains the full conversation of EVERY thread of EVERY project (user prompts, assistant text, thinking text, raw tool args, tool output). The adapter must parse it locally and extract only model id, folder basename, tool label, file basename, thread id - and must never publish `summary` (the model-written thread title). Recommend reading only recently updated rows to limit exposure.

EXTERNAL AGENTS INSIDE ZED: when the user drives Claude Code/Gemini CLI through Zed's Agent Panel, Zed's own row may not carry the raw tool arguments (ACP gives locations/raw_input only), so for those setups the harness-native log (Claude Code ~/.claude/projects JSONL, already supported by Discodex) is strictly better than the Zed adapter.

CONCURRENCY/DB-LOCK: Zed holds the SQLite file open; a shared-lock reader can hit SQLITE_BUSY during Zed's write transactions. Must poll on a background thread with a short timeout and never block the tray/Discord publisher.

LOGO ASSET: the lobehub icon package has no Zed asset, so the logo must come from the upstream repo (tag-pinned jsdelivr URL) - if the tag is deleted the image breaks; keep the org-avatar URL as a fallback.

VERIFICATION GAP (deliberate): per the instruction not to inspect local harness data, no real threads.db was dumped; the on-disk JSON shape is reconstructed from upstream serde structs. The exact nesting of tool_results[].content and the presence/absence of extra fields must be confirmed against a live DB before shipping the parser, and the parser must be written to tolerate both shapes.
confidence: High for the storage/schema facts (all read directly from upstream main-branch source, not from blogs or local machine data). Medium for the adapter design details (per-message blob shape reconstructed from serde definitions only; exact JSON nesting of tool_results[].content not pinned upstream) and for the runtime behaviour of external ACP agents inside Zed.
summary: Zed does store agent activity LOCALLY, but not in a tailable log: the Agent Panel persists every thread in a single SQLite database at %LOCALAPPDATA%\Zed\threads\threads.db (Linux ~/.local/share/zed/threads/threads.db, macOS ~/Library/Application Support/Zed/threads/threads.db). The table `threads` holds one row per thread (id = ACP SessionId, parent_id, folder_paths, summary, updated_at, created_at, data_type, data) where `data` is a zstd-compressed JSON snapshot of the whole thread (DbThread version "0.3.0"). Every save is INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE, i.e. the row is rewritten in place, so there is NO append-only log and no .jsonl anywhere in the Zed repo. Recoverable metadata: workspace folder (folder_paths), model id (model.provider/model), tool name + raw tool input JSON (so file basename via tool input `path`), tool results, thread/parent ids. NOT recoverable: per-message timestamps (messages have no time field; only row-level updated_at/created_at), explicit turn/phase boundaries, an explicit completion marker, and the currently focused editor file (that is editor state, not agent state). Practical consequence: a Zed adapter must open the DB read-only (new dependency: rusqlite with the `bundled` feature, since stock Windows has no system SQLite), zstd-decode each row, and DIFF snapshots per thread id to emit ParsedEvents; the existing LogTailer/recent_logs/parse_line_for(line) contract does not apply. Verdict: partial - all wanted fields are physically present locally, but turn boundaries and the elapsed timer must be inferred (poll latency, seconds) instead of read, completion is heuristic, and External Agents inside Zed may expose only ACP `locations` rather than raw tool args (for those setups the harness-native log, e.g. Claude Code JSONL, is strictly better). Keep the existing focused-app detection for Zed as the fallback.
